COMMUTING REPETITION — FINAL ROOT COMPOSITION AND DEPENDENCY DAG
Status: complete INTERNAL candidate, independent scoped reviews complete.
External certification/formal proof/historical novelty: UNKNOWN.

Exact setting: finite two-player game G, binary acceptance predicate,
arbitrary joint question distribution mu, independent rounds mu^n.
Let d=|A||B|, ell=log d, v=omega_co(G), epsilon=1-v. For a fixed repeated
commuting strategy, a proper coordinate subset C, p=P[win every C]>0,
write tau=(log(1/p)+|C|ell)/(n-|C|), q=mean remaining conditional win and
alpha=1-q. The production proves

  q <= v+4112 tau^(1/4),
  epsilon <= alpha+65536[sqrt(alpha) tau^(1/4)+sqrt(tau)].

The resulting all-wins bound is
  omega_co(G^n)<=exp[-2^(-75) epsilon^3 n/(epsilon+ell)]
for epsilon>0 and all n>=1. epsilon=0 has the trivial bound 1.
The independent scalar threshold deduction gives, for 0<delta<=epsilon,
  P[W>=ceil((v+delta)n)]
     <= exp[-2^(-78) delta^5 n/(epsilon^2(delta+ell))].
Singleton answer alphabets and all-n endpoints are treated separately.
There is no efficient or uniform resource-size assertion.

NONCIRCULAR DAG — read originals by ARTIFACT_ROUTES.json IDs

S: sampler_original + sampler_precision + sampler_toy_required.
Produces actual fixed-resource, all-input commuting left/right POVMs on
finite tracial standard form, using finite trial counts and label cutoffs.
The underlying finite von Neumann algebra itself need NOT be a matrix
algebra. sampler_independent derives a second sampler before exposure;
sampler_audit checks the actual sampler including its operational Section8.
The precision file fixes interpretation of the entire right/opposite label
algebra. The toy addendum is mandatory: exact 1/2 and 2^-N belong to a
separate plain central-projector protocol, not a weighted soft-label filter.
The latter's bad branches are already charged by the core proof.

R: resolvent_production independently reconstructs the raw resolvent and
entropy telescope, then finite scalar-feature normalization. It preserves
EXACT Gram data, referee law Q, conditioning mass p and ideal fine-answer
correlations in a finite amplification of the same algebra. It does not
assume S to prove those identities. No arbitrary Hilbert descriptor and
no finite-matrix density shortcut is used.
